stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is designing a pathway for staff to qualify as pharmacy technicians. Which statements about Board-approved training are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Any training program lasting at least one calendar year automatically qualifies.
A generic Board-approved program must include a minimum of 120 hours of theoretical and 120 hours of practical instruction.
A program provided by a branch of the United States Armed Services or Public Health Service may qualify.
An on-the-job training program may be used only if the pharmacy first obtains a Board waiver.
On-the-job training guidelines must be provided to the Board on request.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 8.02(4) lists qualifying programs, including an ASHP-accredited program, a program provided by a branch of the United States Armed Services or Public Health Service, a Board-approved program with a minimum of 120 hours of theoretical and 120 hours of practical instruction, and any other Board-approved course. 247 CMR 8.06(2) permits pharmacist-led on-the-job training under written pharmacy guidelines, copies of which are provided to the Board on request; no advance waiver is required.

choice_analysis.A: Duration alone is not a qualifying criterion.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: the generic Board-approved route carries that hour split.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: armed services and Public Health Service programs are named.
choice_analysis.D: On-the-job training needs written guidelines, not a Board waiver.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: the guidelines are produced to the Board on request.

related_facts: Completing a Board-approved training program supports the assessment-examination route to licensure.
explanation.mpje_trap: Programme length is not the criterion; the regulation names specific sources and a specific hour split.

reasoning_steps: Match each proposed pathway to the listed program types
Apply the 120-plus-120 hour split to the generic Board-approved route
Treat on-the-job training as guideline-based rather than waiver-based
